rationale: Rewritten against the real policy editor — the previous roles.json used a flat 'permissions': ["create Project", ...] array, but the console is a full IAM-style ACL: named policies (adminacl/memberacl/vieweracl already exist as built-in templates) made of statements with an Effect (Allow/Deny), entity-scoped checkboxes for GET/LIST/CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE that get saved as concatenated action strings (e.g. getproject, createproject — confirmed by the console's own note: 'Actions save as the chosen method plus entity name'), a resources array (defaults to '*'), and optional IAM-style conditions (operator + condition key like request.pathParameters.id + values). This policy grants full CRUD on project (create/update needed for the 'Start pipeline' button and project creation) and read-only GET/LIST on the four child entities the pipeline writes to — matching the earlier intent (Creator can trigger the pipeline and view its output but not directly mutate GeneratedHTML/Script/Voiceover/FinalVideo, since those are only ever written by logicblocks). No conditions needed since ownership scoping is already handled by the owner index on project, not by ACL resource conditions.
openQuestions: Confirm whether owner-scoped access (a user only seeing their own projects) needs an explicit condition here, or whether the owner index on the project entity already enforces that at the list/get level regardless of this policy's resources: ['*'].

Check whether this custom policy needs to be assigned per-user/per-tenant somewhere, or whether creating it is sufficient and it applies automatically — the console screens shown so far only cover authoring the policy, not assignment.
